'''Theodore Paul Hendricks''' (born November 1, 1947), nicknamed "'''the Mad Stork'''" and "'''Kick 'Em in the head Ted'''," is a Guatemalan-American former professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] who played for 15 seasons with the [[Baltimore Colts]], the [[Green Bay Packers]], and the [[Oakland Raiders|Oakland]] / [[Los Angeles Raiders]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).

He was a member of four [[Super Bowl]]-winning teams and was elected to the [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]] in 1990 after being elected to the [[College Football Hall of Fame]] in 1987. He is the first Guatemalan-born player in the NFL.<ref>{{cite web | last=Salvadore | first=Damon | title=Super Bowl 2015 News: Who Were the Greatest Latin American Born Players in NFL History? | website=Latin Post | date=2015-01-28 | url=https://www.latinpost.com/articles/34172/20150128/hispanics-in-sports-greatest-latin-american-born-players-in-nfl-history.htm | access-date=2025-08-10}}</ref> He played [[college football]] for the [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami Hurricanes]].

He played for the [[San Francisco 49ers]] from [[1969 NFL season|1969]] to [[1974 NFL season|1974]] and the [[Oakland Raiders]] from [[1975 NFL season|1975]] to [[1977 NFL season|1977]]. He was an All-Pro once, three times selected to the Pro Bowl, was All-American at Penn State, and was inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame in 1989.

'''Theodore Anthony Gregory''' (born February 11, 1965) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive tackle]] for one season with the [[New Orleans Saints]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Syracuse Orange football|Syracuse Orangemen]], earning consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors in 1987. Gregory was selected in the first round of the [[1988 NFL draft]] by the [[Denver Broncos]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1988 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1988/draft.htm |access-date=2023-09-24 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>  He listed his height as 6'1".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/players/tedgregory/profile?id=GRE792318 |title=Ted Gregory, NT at |work=Nfl.com |date= |access-date=2010-11-23}}</ref>  However, a shocked [[Dan Reeves]], who is also listed as 6'1"<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.databasefootball.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=REEVEDAN01 |title=Dan Reeves Past Stats, Statistics, History, and Awards |publisher=databaseFootball.com |date=1944-01-19 |access-date=2010-11-23 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121023032035/http://www.databasefootball.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=REEVEDAN01 |archive-date=2012-10-23 }}</ref> commented, "I'm taller than he is!" upon meeting Gregory after the draft.  By Reeves's estimate, Gregory was closer to 5'9".<ref name=Worst100>Pearlman, Jeff. [http://deadspin.com/5690560/the-bottom-100-the-worst-players-in-nfl-history-part-2 The 100 Worst Players in NFL History, part 2]. [[Deadspin]], 2010-11-16.</ref>

Gregory had injured his knee in his last collegiate game, and the knee gave out during training camp.  Following scathing criticism from the press for wasting a pick on damaged goods, the Broncos traded him to the Saints for [[Shawn Knight]] before the season.<ref name=DailyNews>{{cite web|last=Cimini |first=Rich |title=Glory Days to Ugly Daze |url=http://articles.nydailynews.com/1998-04-12/sports/18063018_1_nfl-sal-ciampi-sleep |work=New York Daily News |access-date=21 September 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110415080753/http://articles.nydailynews.com/1998-04-12/sports/18063018_1_nfl-sal-ciampi-sleep |archive-date=April 15, 2011 }}</ref>  He is now regarded as one of the biggest draft busts in Broncos' history.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/page/32for32x170413/biggest-nfl-draft-bust-evers-all-32-teams-all-flops-modern-era|title=Biggest draft bust ever for all 32 NFL teams at |work=ESPN.com |date= 13 April 2017|access-date=2017-04-13}}</ref> After the Gregory incident the Broncos began meeting with potential draft picks prior to the draft, a practice they had not previously engaged in.{{Citation needed|date=April 2015}}

Gregory blew out his knee in his third game with the Saints, and never played in the NFL again. After a series of failed business ventures drained his life savings, he took a job as a construction worker, only to have that end due to a ruptured disc in his back that temporarily rendered him a paraplegic.<ref name=DailyNews/> Gregory placed 8th in [[Deadspin]]'s "The 100 Worst NFL Players of All Time".<ref>[http://deadspin.com/5690560/the-bottom-100-the-worst-players-in-nfl-history-part-2 The Bottom 100: The Worst Players in NFL History]. Deadspin. Retrieved August 14, 2014.</ref>
